tools_used: courtlistener MCP: search (dockets), call_endpoint docket-entries (D. Ariz. and CA9 dockets)
WebSearch / WebFetch (supremecourt.gov docket page and respondents' opposition PDF)
pypdf (local text extraction of the fetched opposition PDF)
helpful: Corpus rows carry response_requested / referred_to_court / amicus_briefs, so a conditioned grant rate for the escalation rung could be computed from ~99 resolved substantive priors
Provisioned application.txt had the full argument section and the Ninth Circuit order; the truncation only cut the district-court appendix
CourtListener docket-entries on the CA9 and D. Ariz. dockets confirmed the expedited schedule and the Oct 19 start date
gaps: fedcourts query refuses --limit above 500 at the corpus service with a pydantic error, but --help does not state the cap; two calls were wasted discovering it

No corpus filter for application escalation state (response_requested / referred) or for applicant class (state vs federal vs private): I filtered client-side over broad pulls, which cost ~200 MB of ranged reads on the withdrawn/dismissed sweeps
The statpack interim section publishes no rate conditioned on response-requested; the as-at-prediction conditioned cut had to be built by hand from rows whose flags are as-at-last-poll
WebFetch cannot read a PDF's text; the file was saved locally and extracted with pypdf, which worked but is an unadvertised path
notes: About 22 retrieval calls in total (12 corpus queries including 2 failed on the limit cap, 5 MCP, 5 web). Forward mode; nothing outcome-revealing surfaced.
